characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy focuses on demonstrating the technical viability of alternative authentication methods for Denmark's digital identity infrastructure. Its objectives include developing non-production demonstrators that showcase secure, standards-based access models without reliance on Apple or Google. Key success metrics include the completion of demonstrators, increased policy traction by 15%, and enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations. This lever is crucial for establishing a foundation for platform-neutral access requirements.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes strongly with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as demonstrating technical feasibility provides concrete evidence that can bolster policy proposals. Additionally, it enhances the Coalition Building Strategy by attracting stakeholders interested in credible technical solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Technical Feasibility Strategy may conflict with the Procurement Influence Strategy, as a focus on specific demonstrators could limit the flexibility needed in procurement documents. Additionally, it may constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if the technical focus alienates broader stakeholder interests.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy aims to shape procurement processes by influencing the requirements for Denmark's digital identity systems. It seeks to increase the likelihood of platform-neutral standards being adopted by 20% through targeted policy proposals. Success metrics include the submission of proposals and the degree of influence on AltID requirements. This lever is essential for framing the conversation around digital sovereignty and continuity of service.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy, as a strong coalition can amplify advocacy efforts. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, as demonstrable technical solutions can strengthen policy arguments.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Policy Advocacy Strategy may conflict with the Procurement Influence Strategy if advocacy efforts become too focused on specific privacy arguments, potentially alienating stakeholders who prioritize continuity and supplier concentration risks.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy focuses on strengthening stakeholder engagement to amplify advocacy efforts for platform neutrality in Denmark's digital identity infrastructure. By increasing stakeholder engagement, it aims to create a 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions. Key success metrics include the breadth and diversity of the coalition. This lever is vital for generating political pressure and ensuring a unified front in negotiations.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as a diverse coalition can enhance the impact of policy proposals. It also complements the Technical Feasibility Strategy by attracting stakeholders interested in credible technical solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Coalition Building Strategy may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if the coalition's interests diverge, leading to conflicting priorities that could weaken advocacy efforts. Additionally, it may constrain the Procurement Influence Strategy if coalition members have differing views on procurement language.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy aims to drive the adoption of platform-neutral language in procurement documents for Denmark's digital identity systems. It seeks to achieve a 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity and reduce long-term dependency on major tech platforms. Key success metrics include the inclusion of specific requirements in procurement documents and the establishment of a 'digital sovereignty bonus.' This lever is crucial for ensuring that procurement processes align with the project's goals.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as successful advocacy can lead to more favorable procurement language. It also complements the Coalition Building Strategy by leveraging a strong coalition to push for specific procurement requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Procurement Influence Strategy may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if the focus on specific procurement language limits the flexibility needed for technical demonstrators. Additionally, it may constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if procurement language becomes too technical or specific, alienating broader coalition members.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy focuses on influencing European standards related to digital identity, aiming to enhance interoperability and reduce vendor lock-in. It seeks to provide input to relevant EU bodies and increase alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements by 10%. Key success metrics include active engagement with EU bodies and the successful advocacy for platform-neutral access. This lever is essential for ensuring that Denmark's digital identity initiatives align with broader European frameworks.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as successful engagement with EU standards can bolster national policy efforts. It also complements the Procurement Influence Strategy by ensuring that procurement documents align with European standards.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy may conflict with the Procurement Influence Strategy if the focus on EU standards leads to procurement language that is too rigid or misaligned with local needs. Additionally, it may constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if EU-focused advocacy alienates stakeholders focused on national issues.
